title: Prefetch coordinator off-by-one causing TTFT spike across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Mei Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 we started seeing a reproducible spike in TTFT (first token latency) and a tokens/sec throughput regression across several models in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Root cause analysis indicates an off-by-one error in the prefetch window calculation inside the prefetch/payload coordinator (new heuristic added in runtime-1.19) that caused premature KV-cache invalidations for short-sequence requests and misaligned kernel selection for tiled vs fused attention kernels. This produces cache misses during early steps and extra kernel warmups, increasing median TTFT by ~40-120ms and p95 by ~250-350ms on affected pools; tokens/sec dropped ~15-22% under representative workload mixes. Affected models: Llama-2-13B (fp16/4bit), Falcon-40B, and select quantized variants. Impact vector: Hosted customers saw higher perceived latency; Dedicated pools with conservative batching observed throughput degradation; Private customers with strict latency SLOs filed escalations. Timeline: 2026-03-09 03:40 UTC first signal in runtime dashboards, 03:50 UTC automated regression alert fired, 04:10 UTC customer takedown from support, 04:35 UTC triage started, 07:20 UTC root cause identified, 09:40 UTC hotfix branch cut. This ticket tracks the emergency patch, rollout, and follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: 1) runtime-1.19.1 deployed to canary and reduces median TTFT to within 10% of pre-regression baseline for the tested models; 2) tokens/sec on dedicated pools recovers to within 5% of baseline under the same workload; 3) additional unit/regression tests added to prevent off-by-one in prefetch window; 4) customer-facing incidents updated and customers notified of fix and mitigation steps.
technical_decision_log: 2026-03-09 07:05 - Initial hypothesis: kernel selector heuristic change caused more kernel warmups. Decided to instrument prefetch window counters.

2026-03-09 07:20 - Confirmed off-by-one in prefetch coordinator (window_end computed as start + N instead of start + N - 1). Identified two code paths where KV-cache flush was triggered incorrectly for seq_len <= window_size.

2026-03-09 08:00 - Decision: ship a targeted hotfix to correct prefetch calculation and temporarily roll back the aggressive kernel preference in the selector for canary; do NOT roll back the entire runtime to avoid losing other improvements.
2026-03-09 09:00 - Safety decision: add a runtime flag to disable new coordinator heuristic for customer-managed Private instances until they upgrade to 1.19.1.
2026-03-09 11:15 - Added an integration test that simulates small-sequence traffic mix and validates KV-cache retention across prefetch windows.
actions: Patch prefetch calculation and add bounds checks (PR: infra#4356)
Add regression unit/integration tests for prefetch window and KV-cache invariants
Canary rollout to Hosted us-east-1 and Dedicated small-pool (15% traffic)
Update autoscaling buffer threshold to reduce queueing during rollout (SRE task)
Document workaround for Private customers: set runtime flag 'prefetch_heuristic=stable' until upgrade
Notify affected customers and post incident timeline to status page
Follow-up: run 48h stability window and add dashboard panel for prefetch-miss rate
